walkthroughs.body_html:
Experimental Techniques & Analysis — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Experimental Techniques & Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Experimental Techniques & Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Limewater turns cloudy in the presence of:
options: H₂
O₂
CO₂
Cl₂

mcqs.q: What does a curly arrow in an organic mechanism represent?
options: A curly arrow shows the direction in which heat is flowing in the reaction.
The movement of a pair of electrons from where they are to where they end up.
A curly arrow shows the movement of an atom from one position to another.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.

mcqs.q: What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.
A curly arrow shows the direction in which heat is flowing in the reaction.
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).

mcqs.q: How do alkenes typically react with bromine?
options: By electrophilic addition — bromine adds across the double bond to form a dibromoalkane.
Bromine substitutes for a hydrogen on the alkene, releasing HBr.
A curly arrow shows the direction in which heat is flowing in the reaction.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Formulation”?
options: Single element or compound — a sharp melting/boiling point shows purity.
Lithium (red), sodium (yellow), potassium (lilac), calcium (orange-red), copper (green).
Glowing splint relights.
Useful mixture made to a precise formula, e.g. paints, medicines, fuels.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Test for oxygen”?
options: Useful mixture made to a precise formula, e.g. paints, medicines, fuels.
Turns limewater milky/cloudy.
Glowing splint relights.
Lit splint gives a squeaky pop.
